working_covariance.equation: Let s_i=e_DMbest_i, a=0.5 min_i(s_i)=0.055 mag, b=median_i(s_i)=0.29 mag, G_ig=1(i belongs to group g). Define V=diag(s_i^2-a^2)+a^2*11^T+b^2*GG^T, and C_total=sigma^2 V with sigma>0 dimensionless.
working_covariance.generative_equation: y = X beta + sigma [epsilon + a*z_cal*1 + b*G*z_group], epsilon_i independent N(0,s_i^2-a^2), z_cal~N(0,1), z_group independent standard normals, all mutually independent under this adopted conditional law.
working_covariance.status: a and b are frozen deterministic working choices obtained from released error scales, not published estimates of a physical variance decomposition. The total shape and shared components are explicit assumptions. The fitted sigma makes published errors relative covariance weights for this experiment, not validated total physical error bars.
working_covariance.calibration_accounting: The common a^2 budget is reallocated from the diagonal s_i^2, so diag[diag(s_i^2-a^2)+a^2 11^T]=s_i^2. Do not add a second linewidth, TFR calibration, adjustment-relation uncertainty, or catalogue RMS term. Appendix C already propagates such measured/fitted uncertainty into the reported modulus errors. The actual cross-row calibration covariance is still unknown.
working_covariance.group_pv_accounting: There is exactly one added group-level residual term b^2 GG^T. It is an authored aggregate model for unresolved group/PV-related distance residual dependence. It is not a source-qualified peculiar-velocity covariance or an estimate of velocity dispersion. Source no-double-counting of every physical PV contribution cannot be established from these inputs; retain that physical qualification as HOLD. Do not add another PV draw or covariance on top.
working_covariance.positive_definiteness: s_i^2-a^2 >=0.75*s_i^2>0, so V is strictly positive definite for every group partition. Full274 V is the sole covariance passed to the density and fitted estimator.
working_covariance.low_redshift: Vcmb ranges317..10459 km/s. Log(Vcmb) is only a positive observed covariate in this model. No expansion in v_pec/Vcmb or conversion from Vcmb to a true distance is used, including for PGC9031 at317 km/s.
working_covariance.sensitivity: Do not report a physical bounded covariance/selection sensitivity envelope. No source-qualified bounds were acquired. The exact unrestricted common-zero-point invariance is a mathematical property of this one declared model, not a calibrated physical sensitivity range.

estimation.normalized_factor: F_M(y|beta,sigma)=N_274(y;X beta,sigma^2 V). log F=-0.5[n log(2*pi)+n log(sigma^2)+logdet V+RSS(beta)/sigma^2]. Use Cholesky solves, never an explicit inverse.
estimation.GLS: beta_hat=(X^T V^-1 X)^-1 X^T V^-1 y. n=274, p=rank(X)=7, nu=267. RSS=(y-X beta_hat)^T V^-1(y-X beta_hat). s_hat^2=RSS/nu for intervals; sigma_ML^2=RSS/n for maximum likelihood. Report both with their meanings.
estimation.interval: A=(X^T V^-1 X)^-1. Delta_hat=0.1*beta_hat[width]. SE(Delta_hat)=0.1*sqrt(s_hat^2*A_width,width). The95% interval is Delta_hat +/- t_(267,0.975)*SE. Under the declared Gaussian conditional law the pivot is exactly t_267; this covers the conditional coefficient, not physical distances or survey selection.
estimation.derivation: Whiten by L^-1, V=LL^T. Ordinary least squares in whitened space gives independent Gaussian coefficient error and RSS/sigma^2~chi_square(n-p). The t pivot follows. Adding any constant to y lies in the intercept column, so all other coefficient estimates and residuals are unchanged.

Thus the old report needs clarification: statistical errors already contain calibration-fit contributions, while the full cross-row covariance remains unavailable.

DMbest combines related band estimates; the bands share linewidth information. Section III.4 regularizes distances using Hubble-parameter trends, so this exercise is not an independent validation of a Hubble law.
